97828.q: Apart from uncertain starting values, how do ensembles also take errors in the model itself into account?
a: Through random disturbances in the model physics
By using a coarser grid for all runs
By calculating without the Coriolis force
97828.e: Many ensembles use stochastic physics or different parameterisations. This also captures the uncertainty of the model.
97828.m: Ensembles also disturb the model physics to represent model errors.

97829.q: How does the relative humidity typically change when foehn sets in in a valley north of the Alps?
97829.e: The sinking air warms up without taking up moisture. As a result the relative humidity often falls below 30 %, which increases the risk of fire.
97829.m: Foehn air is warm and very dry.

97830.q: At what speed does a radiosonde balloon typically rise?
97830.e: The amount of gas is chosen so that the balloon rises at about 5 m/s. The ascent to about 30 km therefore takes around 1.5 to 2 hours.
97830.m: A weather balloon rises at about five metres per second.

97831.q: Why do the boiling points of the unbranched alkanes rise as the chain gets longer?
a: The van der Waals forces between the molecules increase
97831.e: Longer molecules have a larger surface area and more electrons. As a result, the van der Waals forces become stronger and more energy is needed to evaporate them.
97831.m: The longer the alkane chain, the higher the boiling point.

97832.q: Which unbranched alkane is the first in the series to be liquid at room temperature?
97832.e: Butane boils at about −0.5 °C and is a gas at 20 °C. Pentane boils at about 36 °C and is therefore liquid.
97832.m: From pentane on, the unbranched alkanes are liquid at room temperature.

97833.q: Why does 2,2-dimethylpropane have a lower boiling point than pentane, even though both are C₅H₁₂?
a: The ball-shaped molecule has less contact area
97833.e: Branched molecules are more compact and touch each other less. So the van der Waals forces are weaker and the boiling point falls.
97833.m: Branching lowers the boiling point of alkanes.

97834.q: Which substance, with an octane number of 100, is the reference for petrol?
97834.e: 2,2,4-Trimethylpentane, also called isooctane, resists knocking very well and is given the octane number 100. n-Heptane is given the octane number 0.
97834.m: By definition, isooctane has an octane number of 100.

97835.q: What is the unbranched alkane with the molecular formula C₇H₁₆ called?
97835.e: Seven carbon atoms give the stem “hept”. With the ending “-ane”, the alkane is called heptane.

97836.q: What is the general molecular formula of the ring-shaped cycloalkanes?
97836.e: Closing the ring needs an extra C-C bond, and two hydrogen atoms are lost in return. Cyclohexane, for example, has the formula C₆H₁₂.
97836.m: Cycloalkanes have two hydrogen atoms fewer than open-chain alkanes.

97837.q: How many oxygen molecules are needed to burn one molecule of propane (C₃H₈) completely?
97837.e: C₃H₈ + 5 O₂ gives 3 CO₂ + 4 H₂O. On the right there are 6 + 4 equals 10 oxygen atoms, so 5 O₂ are needed.
97837.m: One propane molecule burns with five oxygen molecules.

97838.q: Roughly what is the molar mass of hexane (C₆H₁₄) (C: 12.0 g/mol, H: 1.0 g/mol)?
97838.e: 6 · 12.0 g/mol plus 14 · 1.0 g/mol gives 72 + 14 equals 86 g/mol.
97838.m: Hexane has a molar mass of about 86 grams per mole.

97839.q: Why do alkanes practically not dissolve in water?
97839.e: Alkanes contain only non-polar C-C and C-H bonds. They cannot form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.
97839.m: Non-polar alkanes do not mix with water.

97840.q: What is the general molecular formula of alkenes with one double bond?
97840.e: A double bond replaces two hydrogen atoms. So alkenes have two H fewer than the corresponding alkanes.
97840.m: Alkenes have twice as many hydrogen atoms as carbon atoms.

97841.q: According to Markovnikov's rule, which main product forms when HBr adds to propene?
97841.e: The hydrogen atom goes to the double-bond C atom with more hydrogen. This forms the more stable secondary carbocation, and the bromine ends up on the middle C atom.
97841.m: According to Markovnikov, the hydrogen goes where there is already more hydrogen.

97842.q: What is the alkene with the formula CH₂=CH-CH₃ called?
97842.e: Three carbon atoms give “prop”, and the ending “-ene” stands for the double bond. No position number is needed here.
97842.m: Propene is the alkene with three carbon atoms.

97843.q: Which product forms when water is added to ethene?
97843.e: In hydration, an H atom and an OH group add to the double bond. This is how ethanol is made industrially.

97844.q: Which alkene acts as a hormone in plants for ripening fruit?
97844.e: Ripe apples and bananas give off ethene. It speeds up the ripening of nearby fruit.

97845.q: What forms when an alkene reacts with hydrogen and a nickel catalyst?
97845.e: In hydrogenation, hydrogen is added to the double bond. The process is used, for example, to harden fats for margarine.

97846.q: Which test shows double bonds by decolourising purple potassium permanganate?
97846.e: Alkenes are oxidised to diols by potassium permanganate. The purple colour disappears and brown manganese dioxide forms.

97847.q: Which types of bond make up a C=C double bond?
a: One σ bond and one π bond
One ionic bond and one σ bond
97847.e: The σ bond lies on the axis between the atoms, the π bond above and below it. The π bond is weaker and more reactive.
97847.m: A double bond consists of one σ bond and one π bond.

97848.q: Which diene is the building block of natural rubber?
97848.e: Natural rubber is a polymer made of isoprene units. Isoprene has two double bonds.
97848.m: Natural rubber is built from isoprene.

97849.q: What is the general molecular formula of alkynes with one triple bond?
97849.e: Compared with the alkane, a triple bond replaces four hydrogen atoms. That leaves 2n − 2 hydrogen atoms.
97849.m: Alkynes have four hydrogen atoms fewer than alkanes.

97850.q: By which common name is ethyne known?
97850.e: In everyday life, ethyne (C₂H₂) is called acetylene. Ethylene, on the other hand, is the common name of ethene.

97851.q: What is ethyne mainly used for together with oxygen?
97851.e: The flame of ethyne with oxygen reaches over 3,000 °C. It can be used to weld and cut steel parts.
97851.m: Ethyne produces a very hot welding flame.

97852.q: From which solid and water is ethyne produced, for example in a carbide lamp?
97852.e: CaC₂ + 2 H₂O gives C₂H₂ + Ca(OH)₂. The gas produced burns with a bright flame.
97852.m: Calcium carbide gives off ethyne with water.

97853.q: What molecular geometry do the carbon atoms at a C≡C triple bond have?
97853.e: The two σ bonds of each carbon atom point in opposite directions. That is why the atoms H-C≡C-H lie on a straight line.
97853.m: At a triple bond, the molecule is linear.

97854.q: What hybridisation do the carbon atoms in ethyne have?
97854.e: One s orbital and one p orbital each combine to form two sp orbitals. The two remaining p orbitals form the two π bonds.
97854.m: The carbon atoms in ethyne are sp hybridised.

97855.q: Why is ethyne stored dissolved in acetone in gas cylinders?
a: Pure, compressed ethyne can break down explosively
97855.e: Under pressure, ethyne can break down by itself into carbon and hydrogen. Dissolved in acetone in a porous mass, it can be stored safely.
97855.m: Ethyne is stored dissolved in acetone.

97856.q: What is the molecular formula of propyne?
97856.e: Propyne is propane with four hydrogen atoms fewer. It has the structure HC≡C-CH₃.
97856.m: Propyne has the molecular formula C₃H₄.

97857.q: Which group does propan-2-ol belong to?
97857.e: The C atom with the OH group is bonded to two other carbon atoms. So propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol.
97857.m: In secondary alcohols, the OH carbon carries two carbon groups.

97858.q: Why can 2-methylpropan-2-ol hardly be oxidised with mild oxidising agents?
a: There is no hydrogen atom on the C atom with the OH group
It is not soluble in water
97858.e: In tertiary alcohols, the C atom with the OH group carries three carbon groups. Without an H atom there, no C=O group can form.
97858.m: Tertiary alcohols are hard to oxidise.

97859.q: Why is drinking methanol so dangerous?
a: The body turns it into poisonous substances that can cause blindness
97859.e: In the liver, methanol is turned into formaldehyde and formic acid. These damage the optic nerve, among other things.
97859.m: Methanol is dangerously poisonous even in small amounts.

97860.q: How does the solubility of alkanols in water change as the chain gets longer?
a: It first decreases, then increases again
97860.e: The OH group is hydrophilic and the alkyl chain hydrophobic. The longer the chain, the more the non-polar part dominates.

97861.q: Why does ethanol (78 °C) boil at a much higher temperature than propane (−42 °C), which has about the same mass?
97861.e: The OH groups link ethanol molecules through hydrogen bonds. These are much stronger than the van der Waals forces in propane.
97861.m: Hydrogen bonds raise the boiling point of alcohols.

97862.q: Which dihydric alcohol is used as antifreeze in car radiators?
97862.e: Ethane-1,2-diol has two OH groups and mixes well with water. It greatly lowers the freezing point of the cooling water.
97862.m: Ethylene glycol stops cooling water from freezing.

97863.q: What is glycerol called in IUPAC nomenclature?
97863.e: Glycerol has three carbon atoms, each with one OH group. This gives the name propane-1,2,3-triol.

97864.q: Which products form when ethanol reacts with sodium?
97864.e: The sodium replaces the H atom of the OH group. Sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas are formed.
97864.m: Alcohols form alkoxides and hydrogen with sodium.

97865.q: What is the simplest aldehyde called?
97865.e: Methanal has the formula HCHO. Its solution in water is called formalin and is used as a preservative.

97866.q: Which ending do aldehydes have in IUPAC nomenclature?
97866.e: Aldehydes get the ending “-al”, as in ethanal. Alcohols end in “-ol”, ketones in “-one”.

97867.q: Which aldehyde forms when ethanol is mildly oxidised?
97867.e: Ethanol is a primary alcohol. Mild oxidation produces ethanal (acetaldehyde).
97867.m: Primary alcohols are oxidised to aldehydes.

97868.q: What do you observe in a positive Fehling's test with an aldehyde?
97868.e: The aldehyde reduces copper(II) ions to copper(I) oxide. This is precipitated as a brick-red solid.
97868.m: Fehling's test produces red copper(I) oxide.

97869.q: What is the test called in which an aldehyde produces a silver mirror on the glass?
97869.e: The aldehyde reduces silver ions in ammoniacal solution to elemental silver. This is deposited as a mirror.
97869.m: Tollens' test produces a silver mirror.

97870.q: Which class of substances are aldehydes oxidised further to?
97870.e: The aldehyde group -CHO takes up an oxygen atom and becomes the carboxyl group. In this way, ethanal turns into acetic acid.
97870.m: Aldehydes are oxidised to carboxylic acids.

97871.q: Which aromatic aldehyde smells of bitter almonds?
97871.e: Benzaldehyde consists of a benzene ring with a CHO group. It gives the typical smell of bitter almonds and marzipan.

97872.q: Which aldehyde is the main flavour substance of vanilla?
97872.e: Besides the aldehyde group, vanillin has a hydroxyl group and a methoxy group on the benzene ring. Today it is mostly made synthetically.

97873.q: What is the simplest ketone called in IUPAC nomenclature?
97873.e: Propanone (acetone) has three carbon atoms with the carbonyl group in the middle. A ketone needs at least three C atoms.

97874.q: Why does a ketone need at least three carbon atoms?
a: The carbonyl C must be bonded to two other carbon atoms
Ketones always have two C=O groups
97874.e: In ketones, the C=O group is inside the chain. There must be a carbon group on each side.
97874.m: In ketones, the carbonyl group lies between two carbon groups.

97875.q: Which class of substances forms when a secondary alcohol is oxidised?
97875.e: The C atom with the OH group carries two carbon groups. Oxidation creates a C=O group inside the chain, so a ketone.
97875.m: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones.

97876.q: How do ketones behave in Fehling's test?
a: They turn the solution brick red
97876.e: Ketones have no hydrogen atom on the carbonyl C and are not easily oxidised. The blue Fehling's solution stays unchanged.
97876.m: Fehling's test tells aldehydes and ketones apart.

97877.q: What is acetone often used for in the home?
97877.e: Acetone dissolves many synthetic resins and varnishes. It mixes with water and evaporates quickly.

97878.q: What is the ketone with four carbon atoms called?
97878.e: With four C atoms, the carbonyl group can only be on the second C atom. So no position number is needed.
97878.m: Butanone is the ketone with four carbon atoms.

97879.q: Why does acetone (56 °C) boil at a lower temperature than propan-2-ol (82 °C)?
a: Acetone molecules do not form hydrogen bonds with each other
97879.e: Acetone has no H atom bonded to oxygen. Only dipole-dipole forces act, and these are weaker than hydrogen bonds.
97879.m: Ketones boil at lower temperatures than comparable alcohols.

97880.q: What is the equilibrium between a ketone and its form with a C=C double bond and an OH group called?
97880.e: An H atom moves from the neighbouring C to the oxygen and the double bond shifts. With simple ketones, the equilibrium lies almost entirely on the keto side.
97880.m: Ketones are in equilibrium with their enol form.

97881.q: What is the common name of methanoic acid?
97881.e: Methanoic acid (HCOOH) was first obtained from ants. It is also found in stinging nettles.
97881.m: Methanoic acid is also called formic acid.

97882.q: Which carboxylic acid is responsible for the smell of rancid butter?
97882.e: Butanoic acid is released when butterfat breaks down. It smells unpleasantly rancid, which is why it is also called butyric acid.
97882.m: Butyric acid makes rancid butter smell.

97883.q: Which acid is stronger: methanoic acid (pKa 3.75) or ethanoic acid (pKa 4.76)?
a: Neither of them is an acid
97883.e: A smaller pKa means a stronger acid. The methyl group of ethanoic acid pushes electrons towards the carboxyl group and weakens it.
97883.m: The smaller the pKa, the stronger the acid.

97884.q: Because of its structure, which carboxylic acid also gives a positive Tollens' test?
97884.e: In the HCOOH molecule there is a hydrogen atom on the carboxyl C, as in an aldehyde. So methanoic acid acts as a reducing agent and is oxidised to carbon dioxide.
97884.m: Methanoic acid is reducing because of its H atom on the carboxyl carbon.

97885.q: Why do carboxylic acids have especially high boiling points?
a: Pairs of molecules form dimers through hydrogen bonds
97885.e: Two carboxyl groups join through two hydrogen bonds to form a double molecule. More energy has to be supplied to evaporate them.
97885.m: Carboxylic acids form dimers through hydrogen bonds.

97886.q: Which dicarboxylic acid is found in large amounts in rhubarb leaves?
97886.e: Oxalic acid (ethanedioic acid) consists of two linked carboxyl groups. Rhubarb and wood sorrel contain a lot of it.

97887.q: What are the salts of acetic acid called?
97887.e: When acetic acid gives off its proton, the acetate ion CH₃COO⁻ forms. One example is sodium acetate.
97887.m: Salts of acetic acid are called acetates.

97888.q: Which aromatic carboxylic acid is used as the preservative E 210?
97888.e: Benzoic acid stops yeasts and moulds from growing. It consists of a benzene ring with a carboxyl group.

97889.q: Which structural group is typical of esters?
a: -CHO at the end of the chain
97889.e: In an ester, a carbonyl group is joined through an oxygen atom to a second carbon group. This group is called the ester group.
97889.m: Esters have the group -COO- between two groups.

97890.q: Which fruit does 3-methylbutyl acetate (isoamyl acetate) smell of?
97890.e: Isoamyl acetate is an ester of acetic acid and 3-methylbutan-1-ol. It is used as banana flavouring.

97891.q: Which ester of salicylic acid and methanol smells of wintergreen and is found in sports creams?
97891.e: Methyl salicylate is the methyl ester of salicylic acid. It is found in oil of wintergreen and is used in rubs.

97892.q: Chemically speaking, which substances are esters of glycerol and three fatty acids?
97892.e: Glycerol binds three fatty acids through its three OH groups. Such triglycerides are the main components of fats and oils.

97893.q: Why do esters boil at lower temperatures than carboxylic acids of the same molecular mass?
a: Esters do not form hydrogen bonds with each other
97893.e: The ester group lacks the H atom bonded to oxygen. Only weaker dipole-dipole forces act between the molecules.
97893.m: Esters are more volatile than carboxylic acids.

97894.q: What do natural waxes such as beeswax mainly consist of?
a: Esters of long-chain acids and long-chain alcohols
97894.e: In waxes, a long-chain fatty acid is esterified with a long-chain monohydric alcohol. This makes them solid and water-repellent.
97894.m: Waxes are esters of long acids and long alcohols.

97895.q: Which well-known medicine is an ester of acetic acid with salicylic acid?
97895.e: In acetylsalicylic acid, the OH group of salicylic acid is esterified with acetic acid. It relieves pain and lowers fever.

97896.q: Which ester forms from acetic acid and ethanol?
97896.e: In esterification, the acid group of acetic acid reacts with the OH group of ethanol, and water is split off. Ethyl acetate smells fruity and is used as a solvent, for example in nail polish remover.
97896.m: Acetic acid and ethanol form the ester ethyl acetate.

97897.q: How are primary, secondary and tertiary amines distinguished?
a: By the number of carbon groups on the nitrogen
By the number of double bonds
97897.e: A primary amine has one, a secondary two and a tertiary three carbon groups on the N atom. So triethylamine is tertiary.
97897.m: The number of groups on the nitrogen decides the type of amine.

97898.q: Why do amines react as bases in water?
a: The lone pair on the nitrogen takes up a proton
97898.e: Like ammonia, amines bind an H⁺ to their lone pair. This produces hydroxide ions in the solution.

97899.q: Which amine is responsible for the typical smell of fish?
97899.e: Trimethylamine forms when fish protein breaks down. Lemon juice binds it as a salt and reduces the smell.

97900.q: What is the simplest aromatic amine called?
97900.e: Aniline (phenylamine) consists of a benzene ring with an NH₂ group. It was the starting material for many synthetic dyes.
97900.m: Aniline is the simplest aromatic amine.

97901.q: What forms when methylamine reacts with hydrochloric acid?
97901.e: The amine takes up the proton of the acid and becomes the methylammonium ion. With the chloride ion it forms a salt.
97901.m: Amines form ammonium salts with acids.

97902.q: Why does methylamine (about −6 °C) boil at a lower temperature than methanol (about 65 °C)?
a: The N-H hydrogen bonds are weaker than the O-H bonds
97902.e: Nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen. So the hydrogen bonds of amines are weaker.
97902.m: Amines boil at lower temperatures than comparable alcohols.

97903.q: Which functional group does a primary amine have?
97903.e: The amino group consists of a nitrogen atom with two hydrogen atoms. It is bonded to a carbon group.
97903.m: Primary amines have an NH₂ group.

97904.q: Which two amines form when protein rots and have a very unpleasant smell?
97904.e: Bacteria break down the amino acids ornithine and lysine into putrescine and cadaverine. Both are diamines with a strong smell of decay.
97904.m: The smell of decay comes partly from diamines.

97905.q: According to Hückel's rule, how many π electrons must a flat ring contain to be aromatic?
97905.e: A planar, fully conjugated ring is aromatic if it has 4n + 2 π electrons. Benzene meets this with six π electrons.

97906.q: Which aromatic compound made of two joined benzene rings used to be used in mothballs?
97906.e: Naphthalene (C₁₀H₈) consists of two fused benzene rings. It sublimes and has a strong smell.
97906.m: Naphthalene consists of two joined benzene rings.

97907.q: What is the common name of methylbenzene?
97907.e: Toluene is benzene with a methyl group. It is an important solvent and less poisonous than benzene.

97908.q: How many structural isomers of dimethylbenzene (xylene) are there?
97908.e: The two methyl groups can be in the ortho, meta or para position. This gives three isomers.
97908.m: Disubstituted benzenes come in ortho, meta and para forms.

97909.q: Why is phenol more acidic than ethanol?
a: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance in the ring
97909.e: The negative charge of the phenoxide ion spreads over the benzene ring. This makes it easier to release the proton.
97909.m: Phenol is more acidic than ordinary alcohols.

97910.q: Which type of reaction is typical of aromatic compounds?
97910.e: In a substitution, the stable aromatic electron system is kept. An addition would destroy it.
97910.m: Aromatic compounds prefer substitution to addition.

97911.q: Which polycyclic aromatic compound is a highly carcinogenic component of tobacco smoke and charred barbecued food?
97911.e: Benzo[a]pyrene consists of five fused rings. It forms when organic substances burn incompletely.

97912.q: Which aromatic compound with a vinyl group is the building block of polystyrene?
97912.e: Styrene (vinylbenzene) has a C=C double bond next to the ring. It is polymerised through this bond to form polystyrene.

97913.q: Which six-membered ring containing nitrogen is also aromatic?
97913.e: In pyridine, an N atom replaces one CH group of benzene. The ring stays planar with six π electrons.
97913.m: Pyridine is a heterocyclic aromatic compound.

97914.q: Who proposed the ring structure of benzene in 1865?
97914.e: August Kekulé described benzene as a six-membered ring with alternating single and double bonds. He later told of a dream about a snake.
97914.m: Kekulé recognised the benzene ring in 1865.

97915.e: Michael Faraday obtained benzene from the residues of lighting gas. He determined the ratio of carbon to hydrogen.

97916.q: How long are the C-C bonds in benzene compared with single and double bonds?
a: All the same length, in between
All as long as single bonds
All as short as double bonds
97916.e: All six bonds are about 139 pm long. That lies between the C-C single bond (154 pm) and the C=C double bond (134 pm).
97916.m: In benzene, all the ring bonds are the same length.

97917.q: Cyclohexene has an enthalpy of hydrogenation of -120 kJ/mol, benzene one of -208 kJ/mol. Roughly how large is the resonance energy of benzene?
97917.e: For three isolated double bonds you would expect 3 · (-120) = -360 kJ/mol. The difference from -208 kJ/mol is 152 kJ/mol.
97917.m: Benzene is about 150 kJ/mol more stable than expected.

97918.q: Why is benzene hardly used as a solvent any more?
97918.e: Benzene can damage the blood-forming bone marrow and cause leukaemia. It is usually replaced by toluene.

97919.q: Which catalyst is typically used for the bromination of benzene with bromine?
97919.e: Iron(III) bromide is a Lewis acid and polarises the bromine molecule. Only then is it electrophilic enough to react with the benzene ring to form bromobenzene.
97919.m: Benzene only reacts with bromine when a Lewis acid is used as a catalyst.

97920.q: What is the maximum amount of benzene petrol may contain in Switzerland and the EU (as of 2025)?
97920.e: Because of the health risk, the benzene content of petrol is limited to 1 per cent by volume. It used to be much higher.
97920.m: Petrol may contain at most one per cent benzene.

97921.q: At roughly what temperature does benzene boil?
97921.e: Benzene boils at about 80 °C and melts at about 5.5 °C. At room temperature it is a colourless liquid.
97921.m: Benzene boils at about 80 degrees Celsius.

97922.q: What shape is a benzene molecule?
97922.e: All the carbon atoms are sp² hybridised and lie in one plane with the H atoms. The bond angles are 120°.
97922.m: The benzene molecule is a flat hexagon.

97923.q: What is meant by a functional group?
a: A group of atoms that shapes the properties and reactions of a molecule
The longest carbon chain of a molecule
The total number of hydrogen atoms
97923.e: Functional groups such as -OH or -COOH determine chemical behaviour. Organic substances are sorted into classes of compounds according to them.
97923.m: Functional groups determine the class of compound.

97924.q: Which functional group do aldehydes and ketones have in common?
97924.e: Both classes contain a carbon-oxygen double bond. They differ only in its position in the chain.
97924.m: Aldehydes and ketones are carbonyl compounds.

97925.q: Which class of compounds has the general structure R-O-R'?
97925.e: In ethers, an oxygen atom is bonded between two carbon groups. One example is diethyl ether.
97925.m: Ethers have an oxygen atom between two groups.

97926.q: Which class of compounds carries the functional group -CONH₂?
97926.e: In amides, a nitrogen atom is bonded directly to a carbonyl group. Amines lack this C=O group.
97926.m: Amides combine a carbonyl group and nitrogen.

97927.e: Thiols are the sulphur analogues of alcohols. Many smell very strongly even in tiny amounts.

97928.q: Which functional group do nitriles have?
97928.e: Nitriles contain a carbon-nitrogen triple bond. One example is acetonitrile.

97929.q: Which of these groups has the highest priority for the name in IUPAC nomenclature?
97929.e: Carboxylic acids rank above aldehydes, ketones, alcohols and amines. Their group therefore determines the ending of the name.
97929.m: The carboxyl group takes priority in naming.

97930.q: Which two functional groups does lactic acid have?
97930.e: The IUPAC name of lactic acid is 2-hydroxypropanoic acid: “2-hydroxy” stands for the OH group and “-oic acid” for the COOH group. It is a hydroxycarboxylic acid.
97930.m: Lactic acid is a hydroxycarboxylic acid.

98129.e: Wheat is a cereal. Its grains are made into flour for bread.
98129.m: Wheat is the most important bread cereal.

98130.q: Which of these plants is a cereal?
98130.e: Barley is a cereal like wheat, rye and oats. Potato, carrot and pea are vegetables.
98130.m: Barley, rye and oats are cereals.

98131.q: What is a field where grain is grown called?
98131.e: An arable field is a field that is ploughed and planted. On a pasture, by contrast, animals eat grass.

98132.q: What was a flail used for in the past?
a: To beat grains out of the ears
98132.e: With the flail, people beat the ears lying on the floor. This knocked the grains out.
98132.m: In the past, grain was threshed with a flail.

98133.q: Which cereal is polenta cooked from?
98133.e: Polenta is a porridge made from maize semolina. It is especially popular in Ticino.

98134.q: What is left of the grain stalks after threshing?
98134.e: The dry stalks without grains are called straw. Farmers use it, for example, as bedding in the barn.
98134.m: Straw is the dry stalks of cereals.

98135.q: Which cereal is grown most in Switzerland?
98135.e: Wheat grows most on Swiss fields. It is mainly used to make bread.
98135.m: Wheat is grown most in Switzerland.

98136.q: From which part of a cereal grain does a new plant grow?
98136.e: The germ holds the tiny new plant. When the grain gets into damp soil, it starts to grow.
98136.m: The germ is the baby plant in the grain.

98137.q: What does a cereal grain need in the soil to sprout?
98137.e: A grain needs water and warmth to sprout. Then a root and a stalk grow.

98138.q: What is an ear of grain?
98138.e: The ear sits at the top of the grain stalk. The grains grow tightly packed inside it.
98138.m: The grains sit in the ear.

98139.q: What are the long bristles on some ears of grain called?
98139.e: Awns are long, thin bristles on the grains. They stick far out of the ear.
98139.m: The bristles on the ear are called awns.

98140.q: Which cereal has especially long awns?
98140.e: Because of its long awns, an ear of barley looks almost like a paintbrush.
98140.m: You can recognise barley by its long awns.

98141.q: Oats have no ear. What is their flower head called?
98141.e: In oats, the grains hang singly on fine little branches. This kind of flower head is called a panicle.
98141.m: Oats carry their grains in a panicle.

98142.q: What colour is a ripe ear of wheat?
98142.e: Young ears are green. When they are ripe and dry, they turn golden yellow.

98143.q: Which cereal plant carries its grains on a cob?
98143.e: In maize, the grains sit in rows on a thick cob. Wheat, barley and rye have ears.
98143.m: Maize kernels grow on a cob.

98144.q: Why do ripe ears of grain often hang down?
98144.e: When the grains are ripe and plump, the ear becomes heavy. That is why the stalk bends down.
98144.m: Full ears are heavy and droop.

98145.q: What are the grains in the ear for the plant?
98145.e: The grains are the seeds of the cereal. A new plant can grow from every grain.

98146.q: What is made from cereal grains in a mill?
98146.e: In the mill, the grains are ground finely. This makes flour.
98146.m: In the mill, grain is ground into flour.

98147.q: What is the job of someone who grinds grain called?
98147.e: The miller grinds the grain into flour in the mill. The baker then bakes bread from it.
98147.m: The miller grinds, the baker bakes.

98148.q: What used to turn a mill by a stream?
98148.e: The flowing water turned a big wheel. This wheel drove the millstones.
98148.m: A watermill uses the power of water.

98149.q: What is a mill with big sails that turn in the wind called?
98149.e: In a windmill, the wind blows into the sails. This turns the mill without electricity.
98149.m: A windmill is driven by the wind.

98150.q: What was used to grind the grain in old mills?
98150.e: Two heavy, round stones lay on top of each other. The upper one turned and ground the grains.
98150.m: In the past, heavy millstones ground the grain.

98151.q: What do modern mills mostly use to grind grain?
98151.e: Today the grains pass between smooth or grooved steel rollers. This is fast and very fine.
98151.m: Modern mills grind with steel rollers.

98152.q: What are the bits of husk left over from milling called?
98152.e: Bran is made of the outer layers of the grains. For white flour it is separated out.
98152.m: Bran is the ground outer layer of the grain.

98153.q: What does the mill do with the grain before grinding it?
98153.e: First, little stones, dust and other seeds are removed. Only then does the clean grain go for grinding.

98154.q: What is coarsely ground grain, for example for a pudding, called?
98154.e: Semolina is coarser than flour. It is used to cook semolina pudding with milk, for example.
98154.m: Semolina is ground more coarsely than flour.

98155.e: To make flour, cereal grains are ground, for example wheat or spelt.

98156.q: Why is white flour so pale?
a: The outer layer has been removed
98156.e: For white flour only the pale inside of the grain is used. The dark outer layer is separated out.
98156.m: White flour is pale because the outer layer is missing.

98157.q: In Switzerland, what is the dark flour used to bake Ruchbrot called?
98157.e: Ruchmehl contains more of the outer layer than white flour. That is why it is darker.
98157.m: The dark Ruchbrot is baked from Ruchmehl.

98158.q: Which flour is between white flour and Ruchmehl in colour?
98158.e: Half-white flour is a bit darker than white flour but paler than Ruchmehl. It is often used for bread.

98159.q: What is flour mainly made of?
98159.e: Flour consists mostly of starch. It gives the body energy.

98160.q: What is the best way to store flour?
98160.e: Damp flour can go mouldy. If it is well sealed, no small creatures can get in either.
98160.m: Flour must be stored dry and sealed.

98161.q: Which small creature likes to live in old flour supplies?
98161.e: The mealworm is the larva of a beetle. It eats flour and grain.

98162.q: What do you make in a frying pan from flour, eggs and milk?
98162.e: Flour, eggs and milk make a runny batter. It is cooked thinly in the pan.
98162.m: Pancakes are made from flour, eggs and milk.

98163.q: What happens when you stir a little flour into a sauce?
98163.e: When cooked, the starch in the flour binds the water. That is why the sauce gets thicker.

98164.e: For wholemeal flour the whole grain is ground, with its outer layer and germ.
98164.m: Wholemeal means the whole grain is in it.

98165.q: What does wholemeal bread do compared with white bread?
a: It keeps you full for longer
98165.e: The body digests the fibre in wholemeal slowly. That is why you stay full for longer.
98165.m: Wholemeal bread keeps you full for a long time.

98166.q: Where in the grain are there lots of vitamins and minerals?
a: In the outer layer and germ
98166.e: The outer layers and the germ are especially rich in vitamins. In wholemeal bread they are kept.
98166.m: The outer layer and germ are full of vitamins.

98167.q: How can you often recognise wholemeal bread?
a: By bits of husk in the bread
By a hole in the middle
98167.e: In wholemeal bread you often see small dark bits. These are pieces of the grain's outer layer.
98167.m: You can see bits of husk in wholemeal bread.

98168.q: Which bread does the Swiss food pyramid especially recommend?
98168.e: The food pyramid advises choosing wholemeal cereal products. They contain more valuable nutrients.

98169.q: What does yeast do in bread dough?
98169.e: Yeast forms small gas bubbles in the dough. This makes the dough bigger and lighter.

98170.q: What does the yeast produce in the dough that puffs it up?
98170.e: The yeast produces the gas carbon dioxide. It makes lots of small bubbles in the dough.
98170.m: The yeast's gas bubbles make the dough big.

98171.q: Where does a yeast dough rise best?
98171.e: Yeast works best in warmth. In the cold the dough rises only very slowly.

98172.q: What is yeast that you buy as a powder in a sachet called?
98172.e: Dried yeast is yeast that has been dried. It keeps much longer than fresh yeast in a block.
98172.m: Dried yeast is yeast as a powder.

98173.q: What does the yeast in the dough feed on?
98173.e: The yeast eats sugar that comes from the starch in the flour. In doing so it produces gas.

98174.q: Where do the many holes in bread come from?
98174.e: Gas bubbles form while the dough rises. When it bakes, the dough sets and the holes stay.
98174.m: The holes in bread are gas bubbles.

98175.q: What happens to the yeast in the hot oven?
98175.e: The heat in the oven kills the yeast. That is why the bread stops rising after that.
98175.m: Yeast dies in the hot oven.

98176.q: Instead of shop-bought yeast, what can you use to make bread rise?
98176.e: Sourdough is an old, fermenting dough. It makes bread rise and gives it a slightly sour taste.

98177.q: Which four ingredients does a simple bread dough need?
98177.e: For a simple bread, flour, water, salt and yeast are enough. Other ingredients are not needed.
98177.m: Bread needs flour, water, salt and yeast.

98178.q: What do you do with bread dough to make it nice and stretchy?
98178.e: Kneading makes the dough smooth and stretchy. That way it can rise well later.
98178.m: Bread dough must be kneaded well.

98179.q: What does a yeast dough do when it rests covered?
98179.e: During the resting time the yeast works. The dough grows to about twice its size.

98180.q: What do you add when the dough sticks to your hands too much?
a: A little oil in the dough
98180.e: Flour soaks up moisture. That is why the dough sticks less afterwards.
98180.m: A little flour helps against sticky dough.

98181.q: What do you use to roll dough out flat?
98181.e: A rolling pin is a roller made of wood. You use it to roll the dough out thinly.
98181.m: A rolling pin makes dough flat.

98182.q: What do you usually cover dough with while it rises?
98182.e: A cloth keeps the dough warm and stops its surface drying out.
98182.m: A cloth protects the dough while it rises.

98183.q: What is the hard, brown outer layer of a loaf called?
98183.e: During baking, the surface of the dough gets hot and dry. This forms the crispy crust.
98183.m: The crust is on the outside of the bread.

98184.q: What is the soft inside of a loaf called?
98184.e: The crumb is the soft, light part of the bread. You can see the holes from rising in it.
98184.m: Inside the bread is the soft crumb.

98185.q: On which day do people in Switzerland traditionally eat Zopf, a plaited loaf, for breakfast?
98185.e: Zopf is the typical Sunday bread in Switzerland. People like to eat it with butter and jam.
98185.m: Zopf is the Swiss Sunday bread.

98186.q: What goes into Zopf dough but not into a simple bread?
98186.e: Zopf dough is made with milk and butter. That is why Zopf is soft and tastes delicious.

98187.q: What do you brush on the Zopf before baking to make it shiny?
98187.e: Beaten egg is brushed onto the Zopf. In the oven it then turns golden brown and shiny.
98187.m: Brushed with egg, the Zopf shines.

98188.q: How does the Zopf get its shape?
a: It is pressed into a tin
It is rolled into a ball
98188.e: Long strands are formed from the dough. These are plaited together like hair.
98188.m: A Zopf is plaited from strands of dough.

98190.q: Which figure made of sweet yeast dough is baked in Switzerland for St Nicholas Day?
98190.e: The Grittibänz is a little man made of yeast dough, similar to Zopf dough. People eat it around 6 December.
98190.m: On St Nicholas Day there is a Grittibänz.

98191.e: Zopf is a yeast dough. The yeast makes it light and airy.

98192.q: What is the Zopf named after?
98192.e: The loaf looks like plaited hair. In German this hairstyle is also called Zopf.
98192.m: The Zopf looks like plaited hair.

98193.q: Which cereal is spelt closely related to?
98193.e: Spelt is a close relative of wheat. It can be used for baking in a similar way.
98193.m: Spelt is a relative of wheat.

98195.q: What still has to be removed from spelt after threshing?
98195.e: In spelt, the grains stay firmly inside their husks. They have to be removed separately in the mill.
98195.m: Spelt grains sit in tough husks.

98196.q: What is spelt called that is harvested unripe and dried?
98196.e: Green spelt is spelt harvested when half ripe. It is dried and tastes a little smoky.
98196.m: Green spelt is spelt harvested unripe.

98197.q: How long has spelt been grown?
98197.e: Spelt has been grown for thousands of years. It also has a long tradition in Switzerland.

98198.q: What are the tough husks around the spelt grain for?
98198.e: The husks wrap the grain like a protective jacket. They are only removed in the mill.
98198.m: The husks protect the spelt grain.

98199.q: What can you bake with spelt flour?
98199.e: Spelt flour is good for baking. It is used to make bread, Zopf and biscuits.
98199.m: Spelt flour is good for baking.

98200.q: Where does rice very often grow?
98200.e: Many rice fields stand under water. Rice needs a lot of water and warmth.
98200.m: Rice often grows in fields under water.

98201.q: In which canton is the best-known rice field in Switzerland?
98201.e: Rice has been grown near Ascona in Ticino since the 1990s. It is one of the most northerly rice fields in the world.

98202.q: Which dish is cooked with rice?
98202.e: Risotto is a creamy rice dish from Italy that is also popular in Ticino. Polenta is made from maize.

98203.q: What is cooked from rice, milk and sugar?
98203.e: For rice pudding, rice is cooked slowly in milk. With sugar and cinnamon it becomes sweet.
98203.m: Rice pudding is sweet rice in milk.

98204.q: Which group of plants does rice belong to?
98204.e: Rice is a cereal, just like wheat. Its grains grow in a panicle.

98205.q: What is rice called that still has its brown outer layer?
98205.e: Brown rice only has its outermost husk removed. The brown layer stays on.

98206.q: What do people in many Asian countries eat rice with?
98206.e: In China, Japan and Korea people often eat with two chopsticks. You can eat rice well with them too.
98206.m: In East Asia people eat with chopsticks.

98207.q: What do millet grains look like?
98207.e: Millet grains are tiny, round and usually pale yellow. They are much smaller than wheat grains.

98208.q: Where is millet an especially important food today?
98208.e: Millet grows even where it is hot and dry. That is why it is very important in Africa and parts of Asia.
98208.m: Millet grows even in heat and drought.

98209.q: Which cereal can people eat who must not eat gluten?
98209.e: Millet contains no gluten, a protein found in wheat, spelt or barley. Some people get ill from it.

98210.q: What does the magic pot cook in the fairy tale “Sweet Porridge”?
98210.e: In the Brothers Grimm fairy tale, a little pot cooks so much millet porridge that the whole town fills up with it.
98210.m: The fairy tale “Sweet Porridge” is about millet porridge.

98211.q: What did many people in Switzerland often eat made from millet in the past?
98211.e: Before the potato arrived, millet porridge was an important food. Millet is easy to cook.
98211.m: In the past, people often ate millet porridge.

98212.q: Which pets like to nibble at millet sprays?
98212.e: Millet sprays are a popular food for pet birds. The birds peck off the small grains.

a: It is roasted in the oven
98213.e: Millet is cooked in water, similar to rice. Afterwards it is soft and fluffy.

98214.q: Apart from millet grains, what else made from millet can you buy?
98214.e: Millet is also rolled into flakes, similar to oats. You can add them to muesli.

98215.e: The oat grains are warmed and then pressed flat between rollers. This makes flakes.
98215.m: Oat flakes are oat grains rolled flat.

98216.q: Which Swiss breakfast is made with oat flakes and apples?
98216.e: For Bircher muesli, oat flakes are mixed with grated apple, milk or yoghurt.
98216.m: Bircher muesli is made with oat flakes.

98217.q: Which Swiss doctor is Bircher muesli named after?
98217.e: The Zurich doctor Maximilian Bircher-Benner made muesli well known around 1900.
98217.m: Bircher muesli comes from the doctor Bircher-Benner.

98218.q: What is a warm dish of oat flakes cooked in milk called?
98218.e: Porridge is an oat dish. It is a popular breakfast, especially in Great Britain.
98218.m: Porridge is warm oat flakes cooked in milk.

98219.q: Which animal traditionally likes to eat oats?
98219.e: Oats are a classic food for horses. They give them a lot of strength.

98220.q: What are oat flakes made from whole grains called?
98220.e: Jumbo flakes are rolled from whole grains. Fine flakes are made from chopped grains.
98220.m: Jumbo flakes are made from whole oat grains.

98221.q: Why are oat flakes considered a wholegrain product?
a: They contain a lot of sugar
98221.e: For oat flakes, the whole grain with its germ and outer layers is rolled. Only the outer husk is removed.
98221.m: Oat flakes contain the whole grain.

98222.q: What happens to oat flakes when you soak them in milk?
98222.e: The flakes soak up the milk and swell. This makes them soft.

98223.q: What can you bake from oat flakes, butter and sugar?
98223.e: Oat flakes are good for crunchy biscuits. They are mixed with butter, sugar and flour.
98223.m: You can bake biscuits from oat flakes.

98224.q: In a tally chart, how many upright lines do you draw before you draw the line across?
98224.e: You draw four lines next to each other. The fifth line is drawn across them.
98224.m: Four lines and one line across make a group of five.

98225.q: How many groups of five do you need in a tally chart for the number 10?
98225.e: Each group stands for 5. Two groups are 5 plus 5, so 10.
98225.m: Ten is two groups of five.

98226.q: A tally chart shows two groups of five and three single lines. How many is that?
98226.e: Two groups are 5 plus 5, so 10. Add 3 lines and that makes 13.
98226.m: First count the groups, then the single lines.

98227.q: Three groups of five and one single line: which number is that?
98227.e: Three groups are 5 plus 5 plus 5, so 15. With the single line it is 16.
98227.m: You can count groups of five quickly in fives.

98228.q: What do you use a tally chart for?
98228.e: You make a line for every thing you spot. That way you don't lose track while counting.
98228.m: With a tally chart you can easily keep count.

98229.q: Lea counts red cars and ends up with four groups of five. How many red cars did she see?
98229.e: Each group stands for 5. Four groups are 5 plus 5 plus 5 plus 5, so 20.
98229.m: Four groups of five make twenty.

98230.q: Why do you always group five lines together in a tally chart?
98230.e: You can count the groups in fives: 5, 10, 15. That is much faster than counting each line on its own.

98231.q: How do you write the number 7 in a tally chart?
a: One group of five and 2 lines
One group of five and 7 lines
98231.e: One group stands for 5. Then add 2 more lines, because 5 plus 2 is 7.
98231.m: Seven is one group of five and two lines.

98232.q: Tim counts 8 blackbirds and 12 sparrows in the garden. How many more sparrows are there?
98232.e: You work out 12 minus 8. That makes 4.
98232.m: You find the difference with a take-away sum.

98233.q: What are the horizontal lines of a table called?
98233.e: Rows go from left to right, like the lines in a book.

98234.q: What are the vertical lines of a table called?
98234.e: Columns go from top to bottom. Each column often has a heading at the top.
98234.m: Columns run from top to bottom in a table.

98235.q: What is usually at the very top of a table, in the first row?
98235.e: The headings say what is in each column. That way you understand the numbers below.
98235.m: Headings explain what is in the table.

98236.q: A table says: apple 7 children, banana 5 children, pear 3 children. How many children is that altogether?
98236.e: You add all the numbers together: 7 plus 5 plus 3 makes 15.
98236.m: For the total, you add all the values together.

98237.q: What do you call a single box in a table?
98237.e: Where a row and a column meet there is a box. It is called a cell.
98237.m: A box in a table is called a cell.

98238.q: Which plan from school is a table?
98238.e: In the timetable the days are in columns and the lessons are in rows. That is a table.

98239.q: A table says: Monday 3 degrees, Tuesday 7 degrees. How many degrees warmer was it on Tuesday?
98239.e: You work out 7 minus 3. On Tuesday it was 4 degrees warmer.
98239.m: A table makes it easy to compare values.

98240.q: What is a table especially handy for?
a: Writing down data in an orderly way
98240.e: In a table every piece of information has its fixed place. That way you can find everything again quickly.
98240.m: A table brings order to data.

98241.q: What does a longer bar in a bar chart mean?
98241.e: The longer the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
98241.m: A long bar stands for a lot.

98242.q: How do the bars in a bar chart usually lie?
98242.e: In a bar chart the bars lie across. If they stand upright, it is called a column chart.
98242.m: Bars lie down, columns stand up.

98243.q: The bar for dogs is 6 squares long, the one for cats is 4 squares. One square stands for one child. How many more children like dogs?
98243.e: You work out 6 minus 4. Two more children like dogs.
98243.m: You find the difference between two bars by taking away.

98244.q: A bar chart shows: red 5, blue 8, green 3. Which colour has the longest bar?
98244.e: 8 is the biggest number. That is why the bar for blue is the longest.
98244.m: The biggest number gets the longest bar.

98245.q: What does the shortest bar in a bar chart show?
98245.e: A short bar means a small number. So the shortest one shows the least.
98245.m: The shortest bar shows the least.

98246.q: One square in the chart stands for 2 children. A bar is 5 squares long. How many children is that?
98246.e: Five squares times 2 children makes 10 children.
98246.m: Always check what one square stands for.

98247.q: Two bars are exactly the same length. What does that mean?
98247.e: Bars of the same length show the same number.
98247.m: Bars of the same length stand for the same amount.

98248.q: What does every bar need so you know what it stands for?
98248.e: Next to each bar there is a word, for example “dog” or “cat”. Otherwise nobody knows what it means.

98249.q: What do the numbers on the axis of a bar chart show?
a: How old the person who drew it is
98249.e: There is a row of numbers along the axis. You use it to read off which number a bar shows.
98249.m: You read off the values on the axis.

98250.q: What do you do in a survey?
a: You ask lots of people the same question
98250.e: In a survey you ask many people the same thing. Then you count up the answers.
98250.m: In a survey you ask lots of people the same thing.

98251.q: In a class of 20 children, 12 answer yes and all the others answer no. How many say no?
98251.e: You work out 20 minus 12. 8 children say no.
98251.m: The yes and no answers together make all the children.

98252.q: Why may each child answer only once in a class survey?
98252.e: If someone answers twice, their opinion counts twice. Then the result is distorted.
98252.m: Each person counts only once in a survey.

98253.q: What is best to decide before a survey?
a: The question and the answers to choose from
98253.e: If everyone gets the same question with the same answers, the results are easy to count.
98253.m: A good survey has a clear question.

98254.q: How do you quickly note down the answers in a survey?
98254.e: For each answer you make a line in the right row. That way you have counted them all at the end.
98254.m: You count survey answers with tally marks.

98255.q: What do you call what comes out at the end of a survey?
98255.e: After counting, you know how many people gave which answer. That is the result.
98255.m: At the end of a survey there is the result.

98256.q: 25 children are asked: 10 like football, 8 like swimming and the rest like cycling. How many like cycling?
98256.e: 10 plus 8 makes 18. Then you work out 25 minus 18, which is 7.
98256.m: You find the rest by taking away.

98257.q: What do you call the people who answer in a survey?
98257.e: Anyone who is asked and answers is one of the respondents.
98257.m: Respondents give answers in a survey.

98258.q: In a vote with two options, how many votes does the majority have?
98258.e: A majority has more than half of all the votes. It wins the vote.
98258.m: A majority is more than half.

98259.q: There are 24 children in a class. What is the smallest number of votes needed for more than half?
98259.e: Half of 24 is 12. So more than half is at least 13.
98259.m: A majority needs one vote more than half.

98260.q: 15 children want to go to the zoo, 10 children to the woods. Where does the trip go if the majority decides?
98260.e: 15 is more than 10. That is why the zoo has the majority.
98260.m: In a vote, the side with more votes wins.

98261.q: What do you call the smaller group in a vote?
98261.e: The group with fewer votes is the minority.
98261.m: The smaller group is the minority.

98262.q: What is it called when both sides have exactly the same number of votes?
98262.e: When the votes are equal, neither side has the majority. This is called a tie.
98262.m: With equal votes nobody has the majority.

98263.q: When is a proposal accepted in a simple vote?
a: When there are more yes votes than no
When there are more no votes than yes
When only one person says yes
98263.e: If there are more yes votes than no votes, the proposal is accepted.
98263.m: More yes than no means accepted.

98264.q: In which two cantons do people still vote by raising their hands at an open-air assembly, the Landsgemeinde?
98264.e: At the Landsgemeinde the voters gather outdoors. The majority of raised hands is counted.
98264.m: Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden have a Landsgemeinde.

98265.q: Out of 9 children, 5 vote yes. Do the yes votes have the majority?
98265.e: Half of 9 is four and a half. 5 is more than four and a half, so it is a majority.
98265.m: With 9 votes, 5 is enough for a majority.

98266.q: Rolling a 7 with an ordinary dice: what is that?
98266.e: An ordinary dice only has the numbers 1 to 6. So you can never roll a 7.
98266.m: There is no 7 on an ordinary dice.

98267.q: The sun will rise again tomorrow morning. What is that?
98267.e: The Earth turns once every day. That is why the sun rises every morning, even if clouds hide it.
98267.m: Something that always happens is certain.

98268.q: A little bag holds 9 red balls and 1 blue one. Which colour will you probably pick?
98268.e: There are many more red balls than blue ones. That is why red is much more likely.
98268.m: You are more likely to pick what there is more of.

98269.q: A little bag holds only red balls. What is picking a red ball?
98269.e: There is no other colour in the bag. Every ball you pick is red.
98269.m: If only red is inside, you are certain to pick red.

98270.q: How likely is it to snow in the city of Zurich in July?
98270.e: In July it is usually warm in Zurich. Snow in the city practically never happens then.
98270.m: Something that hardly ever happens is unlikely.

98271.q: You toss a coin. Which is more likely, heads or tails?
98271.e: A coin has two sides. Each side is just as likely to land on top.
98271.m: With a coin, heads and tails are equally likely.

98272.q: A little bag holds 3 green and 3 yellow balls. Which colour are you more likely to pick?
98272.e: There are the same number of balls of each colour. So neither colour is more likely.
98272.m: The same number of balls means the same chance.

98273.e: Impossible means that something cannot happen in any case.
98273.m: Impossible is the opposite of certain.

98274.q: A spinner has 4 equal sections: 3 red and 1 blue. Where is it more likely to stop?
98274.e: Three of the four sections are red. That is why the spinner is more likely to stop on red.
98274.m: More sections of one colour means more chances.

98275.q: What do the dots on two opposite sides of a dice add up to?
98275.e: On an ordinary dice, opposite sides always add up to 7. For example, the 3 is opposite the 4.
98275.m: Opposite sides of a dice add up to seven.

98276.q: Which number is opposite the 1 on a dice?
98276.e: Opposite sides add up to 7. 7 minus 1 is 6.
98276.m: The six is opposite the one.

98277.q: How many corners does a dice have?
98277.e: A dice has four corners at the top and four at the bottom. That makes 8 altogether.

98278.q: How many dots does a dice have on all six sides together?
98278.e: You work out 1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4 plus 5 plus 6. That makes 21.
98278.m: All the dots on a dice add up to 21.

98279.q: You roll two dice. What is the biggest total you can roll?
98279.e: The highest number on a dice is 6. Two sixes make 12 together.
98279.m: With two dice you can roll at most twelve.

98280.q: You roll two dice. What is the smallest total possible?
98280.e: The smallest number on a dice is 1. Two ones make 2 together.
98280.m: With two dice you roll at least two.

98281.q: What are the dots on a dice called?
98281.e: The dots on a dice are called pips. For example, you say: “I rolled six pips.”
98281.m: The dots on a dice are called pips.

98282.q: Who is in 1st place on a results list?
98282.e: Whoever did best is in 1st place. He or she has won.

98283.q: In the sprint, Ana runs 9 seconds, Ben 8 seconds and Cem 10 seconds. Who wins?
98283.e: In running, whoever takes the least time wins. Ben only takes 8 seconds.
98283.m: In a race, the shortest time wins.

98284.q: In the long jump, Mia jumps 3 metres, Noah 2 metres 50 and Lina 3 metres 20. Who is in 1st place?
98284.e: In the long jump, the furthest jump wins. 3 metres 20 is the furthest.
98284.m: In the long jump, the longest jump wins.

98285.q: Lia is in 2nd place, Max in 4th. How many children are between them on the results list?
98285.e: Between 2nd and 4th place there is only 3rd place. There is one child there.

98286.q: How many people stand on the podium at a medal ceremony?
98286.e: The top three stand on the podium. The winner stands highest in the middle.
98286.m: The top three stand on the podium.

98287.q: Which medal do you usually get for 2nd place?
98287.e: 1st place gets gold, 2nd place silver and 3rd place bronze.

98288.q: Which medal do you usually get for 3rd place?
98288.e: The bronze medal is for third place.

98289.q: Five children have a race. What place is the slowest child in?
98289.e: With five children there are places 1 to 5. The slowest child comes last, so in 5th place.
98289.m: With five people taking part, 5th place is last.

98290.q: What is the average of 2 and 4?
98290.e: 2 plus 4 makes 6. Divided by 2 numbers, that makes 3.
98290.m: The average is in the middle.

98291.q: What is the average of 3, 5 and 7?
98291.e: 3 plus 5 plus 7 makes 15. 15 divided by 3 makes 5.

98292.q: What is the average of 10 and 20?

98293.q: What is the first thing you do when working out an average?
98293.e: First you add all the numbers together. Only then do you carry on working with this total.
98293.m: For the average, you first add everything together.

98294.q: You have added all the numbers together. What do you divide the total by to get the average?
a: By how many numbers there are
98294.e: You divide by how many numbers there are. With three numbers you divide by 3.
98294.m: You divide the total by the number of values.

98295.q: A team scores 1, 2 and 3 goals in three matches. How many goals is that on average per match?
98295.e: 1 plus 2 plus 3 makes 6 goals. 6 divided by 3 matches makes 2.
98295.m: On average two goals were scored per match.

98296.q: What is the average of 4, 4 and 4?
98296.e: If all the numbers are the same, the average is exactly that number. 12 divided by 3 makes 4.
98296.m: If all the numbers are the same, the average is that same number.

98297.q: In the morning it is 6 degrees, at midday 8 degrees and in the evening 10 degrees. What is the average temperature?
98297.e: 6 plus 8 plus 10 makes 24. 24 divided by 3 makes 8 degrees.
98297.m: You can find the average of temperatures too.

98298.q: In a pictogram, one apple picture stands for 2 apples. How many apples do 4 apple pictures show?
98298.e: Each picture stands for 2 apples. 4 times 2 makes 8.
98298.m: You multiply the pictures by their value.

98299.q: One stick figure in a pictogram stands for 5 children. How many children do 3 stick figures show?
98299.m: Three figures of five children each make fifteen children.

98300.q: A whole picture stands for 10 bikes. How many bikes does half a picture show?
98300.e: Half of 10 is 5. So half a picture stands for 5 bikes.
98300.m: Half a picture shows half the amount.

98301.q: What colour is the sign with the running figure that shows the emergency exit?
98301.e: Safety signs like the emergency exit are green with a white picture.
98301.m: The emergency exit sign is green.

98302.q: Why are there lots of pictograms at stations and airports?
a: You can understand them without language
98302.e: There are people from many countries at stations. Everyone understands a picture, even if they don't speak the language.
98302.m: Pictograms are understood in every language.

98303.q: What does a pictogram with a knife and fork mean?
a: You can get something to eat here
98303.e: You need a knife and fork for eating. The sign shows a restaurant or a snack bar.
98303.m: A knife and fork show a place to eat.

98304.q: What must always be shown with a pictogram chart?
98304.e: Without this information you don't know whether a picture stands for 1, 2 or 10.
98304.m: A pictogram chart needs a key to explain the pictures.

98305.e: February has only 28 days, sometimes one more. All the other months have 30 or 31 days.

98306.q: How many days does February have in a leap year?
98306.e: In a leap year, February gets an extra day. It then has 29 days.
98306.m: In a leap year February has 29 days.

98307.q: What do you call a list in which you write down the weather every day?
98307.e: In a weather diary you note down things like the temperature, clouds and rain every day. That way you can compare later.
98307.m: In a weather diary you collect weather data.

98308.q: Why do you hang a thermometer for the air temperature in the shade?
a: The sun would heat it up extra
98308.e: In the sun the thermometer itself gets warm. Then it shows a higher reading than the air really is.
98308.m: Air temperature is measured in the shade.

98309.q: In one week it rains on 2 days. On how many days does it stay dry?
98309.e: A week has 7 days. 7 minus 2 makes 5 dry days.
98309.m: The days with and without rain together make a week.

98310.q: Why is it best to measure the temperature at the same time every day?
a: So you can compare the days
Because that is the rule in the garden
98310.e: At midday it is usually warmer than in the morning. If you always measure at the same time, you can compare the days fairly.
98310.m: Measuring at the same time makes values comparable.

98311.q: A weather diary shows: Mon sun, Tue rain, Wed sun, Thu sun, Fri rain. On how many days did the sun shine?
98311.e: The sun shone on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. That is 3 days.
98311.m: In a weather diary you can count up the days.

a: How strongly the wind is blowing
98312.e: An anemometer often has little cups that spin in the wind. The faster they spin, the stronger the wind.
98312.m: The anemometer shows the wind strength.

98313.q: Midday temperatures: Monday 10 degrees, Tuesday 14 degrees, Wednesday 12 degrees. Which day was the warmest?
98313.e: 14 degrees is the highest number. So Tuesday was the warmest.
98313.m: The highest temperature shows the warmest day.

98314.q: What do you look at if you want to note down whether it is cloudy?
98314.e: You can see in the sky whether it is cloudy. You estimate how much of it is covered with clouds.
98314.m: You observe cloud cover in the sky.

98315.q: How do you often notice that you are tired?
98315.e: When the body needs sleep, the eyelids get heavy and almost close by themselves.
98315.m: Heavy eyes show you that you need sleep.

98316.q: What helps best against tiredness in the evening?
98316.e: Only real sleep helps against tiredness. During sleep, the body and brain recover.
98316.m: If you are tired, you should go to bed.

98317.q: How do you often feel when you have not slept enough?
98317.e: Too little sleep makes you tired and often irritable too. You have less strength and patience.
98317.m: Too little sleep makes you tired and grumpy.

98318.q: What often happens at school when you are very tired?
a: You find it hard to concentrate
98318.e: A tired brain works more slowly. You cannot pay attention as well and remember less.

98319.q: Which drink contains caffeine, which keeps you awake and is not good for children?
98319.e: Cola contains caffeine. Caffeine keeps you awake and can make it harder to fall asleep.
98319.m: The caffeine in cola keeps you awake.

98320.q: Why is it dangerous to ride a bike when you are very tired?
98320.e: If you are tired, you react more slowly and miss dangers more easily. That can lead to accidents in traffic.
98320.m: When tired, you react too slowly in traffic.

98321.q: What does your body do while you sleep?
98321.e: During sleep the body rests and repairs itself. In the morning you are refreshed again.
98321.m: Your body recovers while you sleep.

98322.q: What is the hormone that makes us tired in the evening called?
98322.e: Melatonin is made in the body when it is dark. It tells the body that it is time to sleep.

98323.q: How can you tell that you have had enough sleep?
a: You wake up fit in the morning
You are very tired at lunchtime
98323.e: If you sleep enough, you wake up refreshed and stay awake and lively during the day.
98323.m: If you sleep enough, you are fit in the morning.

98324.q: What do you call a short sleep in the middle of the day?
98324.e: An afternoon nap is a short sleep after lunch. Many small children have one every day.
98324.m: A short sleep in the middle of the day is a nap.

98325.q: In which country is the “siesta”, a midday rest, especially well known?
98325.e: The siesta is a midday rest in Spain. Many people rest there during the hot middle of the day.
98325.m: The siesta is the Spanish midday rest.

98326.q: Who most often needs an afternoon nap?
98326.e: Toddlers need a great deal of sleep. That is why they usually sleep in the middle of the day too.

98327.q: Roughly how long should a short nap for adults last?
98327.e: A short nap of about 10 to 30 minutes is refreshing. If you sleep longer, you often wake up groggy.
98327.m: A short nap only lasts about 20 minutes.

98328.q: Why should a nap not be too long?
a: Otherwise you find it harder to fall asleep at night
Otherwise you get ill straight away
98328.e: If you sleep a long time during the day, you are less tired in the evening. Then falling asleep is harder.
98328.m: A long nap disturbs your night's sleep.

98329.q: What is another word for a short sleep during the day?
98329.e: A nap is a short, light sleep during the day. You often nod off.
98329.m: A nap is a short sleep.

98330.q: Up to what age do most children have an afternoon nap?
98330.e: Most children stop having an afternoon nap between 3 and 5. Then the sleep at night is enough for them.
98330.m: At about 3 to 5, children stop having an afternoon nap.

98331.q: Which place is good for a nap?
a: A room with a loud television
98331.e: Quiet and little light help you fall asleep. Noise and bright light keep you awake.
98331.m: Quiet and darkness help with a nap.

98332.q: When do children often have more nightmares?
a: When they have had a bath
98332.e: Worries and excitement keep the brain busy at night too. That is why nightmares happen more often at such times.
98332.m: If you have worries, you have bad dreams more often.

98333.q: What can you do if you wake up after a nightmare?
98333.e: Parents can comfort and calm you. Afterwards you can usually fall asleep again easily.
98333.m: After a nightmare, it is fine to look for comfort.

98334.q: Do many children sometimes have nightmares?
98334.e: Almost all children have nightmares now and then. That is normal and not dangerous.
98334.m: Nightmares are completely normal in children.

98335.q: Is a monster from a nightmare real?
a: Yes, it lives under the bed
98335.e: Dreams happen in your head. What you dream has not really happened.
98335.m: What you dream is not real.

98336.q: What helps you calm down after a nightmare?
98336.e: Calm, deep breathing relaxes the body. Your heart then beats more slowly again.
98336.m: Deep breathing calms you after a nightmare.

98337.e: A nightmare is a dream that frightens you. You often wake up from it with a start.
98337.m: A nightmare is a dream that frightens you.

98338.q: What can cause nightmares in the evening?
98338.e: Scary pictures stay in your head. At night they can turn up again in dreams.
98338.m: Scary films in the evening can bring nightmares.

98339.q: Where does the “mare” in “nightmare” come from?
a: From a night spirit in old legends
98339.e: In old legends, a mare was a night spirit. People believed it sat on the chest of sleeping people at night.
98339.m: In old legends, the mare was a night spirit.

98340.q: What do you call the loud, rumbling breathing noise during sleep?
98340.e: When you snore, breathing during sleep makes a loud, rumbling noise.
98340.m: Loud breathing in your sleep is called snoring.

98341.q: Why does snoring make a noise?
98341.e: During sleep, the muscles in the throat relax. The air makes soft parts of the throat flutter, and that makes the noise.
98341.m: When you snore, soft parts of the throat flutter.

98342.q: When do people snore more often?
98342.e: If your nose is blocked, you breathe through your mouth. Then you snore more easily.
98342.m: With a blocked nose you snore more easily.

98343.q: In which position do many people snore most?
98343.e: Lying on your back, the tongue falls back a little. Then the throat gets narrow and you are more likely to snore.
98343.m: You snore most lying on your back.

98344.q: Which of these animals can also snore?
98344.e: Dogs also breathe through the nose and throat and can snore in their sleep, especially dogs with short noses.

98345.q: Who snores more often on average?
98345.e: Adult men snore more often than women and children.
98345.m: Men snore more often than women.

98346.e: The person snoring is asleep and usually does not hear it. The others in the room hear it all the better.
98346.m: It is usually the others who hear the snoring.

98347.q: Which little flap at the back of the mouth often flutters when you snore?
98347.e: The uvula hangs at the back of the roof of the mouth. When you snore, it can flutter together with the soft palate.
98347.m: The uvula hangs at the back of your mouth.

a: Something you do the same way every evening
98348.e: A bedtime routine is a fixed set of steps before sleeping, the same every evening. It helps you calm down.
98348.m: A bedtime routine is the same every evening.

98349.q: What is a good bedtime routine?
98349.e: A calm story is relaxing. Exciting films and wild games, on the other hand, wake you up.
98349.m: A bedtime story helps you fall asleep.

98350.q: What should you do every evening before going to sleep?
98350.e: Before sleeping you brush your teeth. That way they stay clean and healthy overnight.
98350.m: You brush your teeth before going to sleep.

98351.q: Why does a bedtime routine help?
a: The body notices that it is time to sleep
98351.e: If you do the same thing every evening, your body gets used to it. It then knows that it will soon be time to sleep.
98351.m: A fixed routine shows the body that it is time to sleep.

98352.q: What is a song that you sing to children to help them fall asleep called?
98352.e: A lullaby is a calm song for falling asleep. In the past it was sung while rocking the baby's cradle.
98352.m: You sing a lullaby to help someone fall asleep.

98353.q: Which animals do people often count when they cannot fall asleep?
98353.e: Counting sheep is an old tip. The steady counting is boring and is meant to make you tired.
98353.m: If you cannot fall asleep, you count sheep.

98354.q: Is it good to go to bed at about the same time every evening?
a: Yes, it helps you fall asleep
98354.e: Fixed bedtimes help your body clock. Then you get tired at the right time every evening.
98354.m: Fixed bedtimes help you fall asleep.

98355.q: Which drink suits an evening routine well?
98355.e: Warm milk contains no caffeine and is nicely warming. Drinks with caffeine, on the other hand, can keep you awake.
98355.m: In the evening it is better not to drink anything with caffeine.

98356.q: What do people often say to each other before going to sleep?
98356.e: With “Good night” you wish each other a good sleep. In many families it is part of the evening.
98356.m: Before going to sleep, people say “Good night”.

98357.q: Which cuddly toy is named after an American president?
98357.e: The teddy bear is named after President Theodore “Teddy” Roosevelt. It has been very popular for over 100 years.
98357.m: The teddy bear has a president's nickname.

98358.q: Why do many children have a cuddly toy in bed?
a: It comforts them and makes them feel safe
It wakes them in the morning
98358.e: A cuddly toy is familiar and soft. That gives a safe feeling at night.
98358.m: A cuddly toy gives a safe feeling.

98359.q: How can you clean a dirty cuddly toy?
98359.e: Many cuddly toys can be washed in the washing machine, best in a laundry bag. But you should check the label first.
98359.m: You can wash a dirty cuddly toy.

98360.q: What are most cuddly toys made of?
98360.e: Cuddly toys are made of soft fabric and filled with stuffing. That is why they are nice to squeeze.
98360.m: Cuddly toys are made of soft fabric.

98361.q: What is another name for a cuddly toy made of fluffy fabric?
98361.e: Plush is a soft fabric with short, fluffy hairs. That is why cuddly toys are often called plush toys.
98361.m: A fluffy cuddly toy is also called a plush toy.

98362.q: What is a small, soft cloth for babies, often with an animal's head, called?
98362.e: A comforter is soft and small. Babies like to hold it tight as they fall asleep.
98362.m: Babies like to cuddle a comforter.

98363.q: What do you do if your cuddly toy has a hole?
a: Put it out in the rain
98363.e: With a needle and thread you can sew up a hole in the fabric. Then no more stuffing falls out.
98363.m: You can sew up a hole in a cuddly toy.

98364.q: What kind of animal is Winnie the Pooh?
98364.e: Winnie the Pooh is a teddy bear from children's books. Eeyore the donkey and Tigger the tiger are his friends.
98364.m: Winnie the Pooh is a bear.

98365.q: What is a night light for?
a: It gives a little light in the dark
It wakes you in the morning
98365.e: A night light glows faintly at night. That way you can find your way in the dark.
98365.m: A night light glows faintly at night.

98366.q: Which light is better for sleep at night?
98366.e: Bright light wakes you up. A faint, warm light disturbs your sleep the least.
98366.m: At night, faint warm light is best.

98367.q: When does a night light with a sensor switch on?
98367.e: A light sensor notices when it gets dark. Then the night light comes on by itself.
98367.m: A night light with a sensor comes on in the dark.

98368.q: Why do many children like a night light?
a: They are less afraid of the dark
98368.e: Many children are scared in a completely dark room. A small light is calming.
98368.m: A night light takes away the fear of the dark.

98369.q: Which object in the sky is a natural night light?
98369.e: The moon is lit up by the sun and so it shines at night. At full moon it is quite bright outside.
98369.m: The moon is the night light in the sky.

98370.q: What does a night light without a cable need?
98370.e: Without a cable, a lamp needs a battery or a rechargeable battery. The power is stored in it.
98370.m: A night light without a cable needs a battery.

98371.q: In what kind of room does the body sleep best?
a: With a torch shining in your face
98371.e: Darkness tells the body that it is night. That is why you sleep most deeply in the dark.
98371.m: The body sleeps best in the dark.

98372.q: Where do you often plug in a small night light?
98372.e: Many night lights plug straight into the socket. That way they get power and glow.
98372.m: Many night lights plug into the socket.

98373.q: What often happens when you see someone yawn?
98373.e: Yawning is catching. Often it is enough just to see someone yawn or to read about it.

98374.q: When do we yawn especially often?
98374.e: In the evening and in the morning we are tired. Then we yawn especially often.
98374.m: If you are tired, you yawn often.

98375.q: What do we do with our mouth when we yawn?
98375.e: When we yawn, we open our mouth wide and breathe in deeply. Then we breathe out slowly.
98375.m: When you yawn, you open your mouth wide.

98376.e: Many animals with a backbone yawn, for example lions, cats and monkeys.

98377.q: Roughly how long does a yawn last?
98377.e: A yawn lasts about 6 seconds on average. So it is over quickly.
98377.m: A yawn only lasts a few seconds.

98378.q: What do you do out of politeness when you yawn?
a: Put your hand in front of your mouth
Sing loudly at the same time
98378.e: You hold your hand in front of your open mouth. That is considered polite.
98378.m: When you yawn, you put your hand in front of your mouth.

98379.q: Apart from tiredness, when else do we often yawn?
98379.e: Boredom also makes us yawn. Many people know this from long waits.

98380.q: What do people often do together with yawning when they wake up?
98380.e: After waking up, many people yawn and stretch their arms and legs. That wakes the muscles up.
98380.m: After waking up, you yawn and stretch.

98381.q: What is it called when someone gets up and walks around in their sleep?
98381.e: When sleepwalking, someone gets up in their sleep and walks around without really being awake.
98381.m: Someone who walks around in their sleep is sleepwalking.

98382.e: Sleepwalking happens much more often in children than in adults.

98383.q: Does a sleepwalker remember it in the morning?
98383.e: Sleepwalkers are not really awake. That is why they usually know nothing about it in the morning.
98383.m: Sleepwalkers usually do not remember it.

98384.q: What should you do with a sleepwalker?
a: Calmly lead them back to bed
98384.e: You gently lead a sleepwalker back to bed. You should not frighten them.
98384.m: You calmly lead a sleepwalker back to bed.

98385.q: What are the eyes often like during sleepwalking?
98385.e: Sleepwalkers often have their eyes open. Even so, they are asleep and staring into space.
98385.m: Sleepwalkers often have their eyes open.

98386.q: Does sleepwalking in children usually stop again?
98386.e: In most children, sleepwalking stops by itself by the teenage years.

98387.q: What protects a sleepwalker from accidents?
a: Stretching a rope across the room
98387.e: Safe stairs and windows prevent falls. Things lying around should be tidied away.
98387.m: Safe stairs and windows protect sleepwalkers.

98388.q: Is a sleepwalker awake while walking around?
98388.e: Sleepwalking happens in deep sleep, usually in the first half of the night. That is why the sleepwalker notices nothing.

98389.q: What can make sleepwalking happen more often?
98389.e: Lack of sleep can trigger sleepwalking. So getting enough sleep helps against it.

98390.q: Mia sleeps 10 hours every night. How many hours does she sleep in a week?
98390.e: A week has 7 nights. 7 times 10 hours makes 70 hours.

98391.q: How many hours of sleep do adults need each night?
98391.e: Adults are advised to get 7 to 9 hours of sleep a night.
98391.m: Adults need 7 to 9 hours of sleep.

98392.e: Newborn babies sleep about 14 to 17 hours a day, spread over lots of little naps.

98393.q: Roughly how much of their life do people spend asleep?
98393.e: If you sleep 8 out of 24 hours, you sleep a third of the day. So you spend about a third of your life asleep.
98393.m: We spend about a third of our lives asleep.

98394.q: Which animal sleeps up to 20 hours a day?
98394.e: Koalas eat eucalyptus leaves, which provide little energy. That is why they sleep and rest for up to 20 hours a day.
98394.m: The koala is a great sleeper.

98395.q: Tim gets up at 7 o'clock and wants to sleep for 10 hours. When does he need to go to bed?
98395.e: From 9 pm to 7 am is 10 hours. You work out 7 o'clock minus 10 hours.
98395.m: If you get up early, you need to go to bed early.

98396.q: Lea sleeps from 8 pm to 7 am. How many hours is that?
98396.e: From 8 pm to midnight is 4 hours, from midnight to 7 am is 7 hours. 4 plus 7 makes 11 hours.
98396.m: You add up the hours of sleep across midnight.

98397.q: How many hours of sleep do teenagers aged 13 to 18 need?
98397.e: Teenagers need about 8 to 10 hours of sleep, a bit more than adults.
98397.m: Teenagers need 8 to 10 hours of sleep.

98398.q: What are the clothes you put on to sleep called?
98398.e: Pyjamas are comfortable clothes for the night. You put them on before going to sleep.

98399.q: In which country do pyjamas have their origin?
98399.e: Pyjamas originally come from India and its neighbouring countries. The British brought them to Europe.

98400.q: Which two parts do pyjamas usually have?
98400.e: Pyjamas usually have a top and long or short trousers.
98400.m: Pyjamas have a top and trousers.
